title: Capstone: the store scorecard
summary: Build a one-row-per-store scorecard from a weekly sales log, combining SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, XLOOKUP, ROUND and IF into a final rating.

blocks.text: The area manager wants one row per store: total sales, how many weeks were good, the store's target, achievement against target and a single rating she can read at a glance.
All the facts are already on the sheet, in a weekly log and a target table. Your job is to pull them together with the skills you have built so far.

items: Objective: combine SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, XLOOKUP, ROUND, AND and IF into one scorecard with a final rating.
You pass the mission at 75% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.text: SUMIFS adds the numbers in the first range for the rows where the criteria range matches. =SUMIFS($C$2:$C$13,$A$2:$A$13,H2) totals the sales of the store named in H2.

COUNTIFS counts the rows where every condition is true. =COUNTIFS($A$2:$A$13,H2,$C$2:$C$13,">="&$I$7) counts this store's weeks at or above the good-week level in I7. The & joins the text >= to the number in I7.
XLOOKUP finds the store name in the target table and returns its target. It follows the name, not the row position.
Achievement % = total sales divided by target, times 100, rounded to 1 decimal place.

AND is TRUE only when both conditions are true. A store is a Star when achievement and good weeks both reach their levels. Otherwise it is Watch if achievement is at least the watch level, and Action if not.

blocks.caption: Rating rules used in this mission
rows: Achievement at or above the Star level AND enough good weeks
Not a Star, but achievement at or above the Watch level

blocks.text: Tip: lock the log and table ranges with $ signs so every row of the scorecard reads the same data. Keep the rules in cells I7:I10 so the area manager can change them without touching a formula.
Four questions on the scorecard. Type numbers without commas, for example 150.

items: SUMIFS adds numbers for rows that match, and COUNTIFS counts rows that match all conditions.
">="&cell builds a condition from a rule stored in a cell.
XLOOKUP pulls a value from a table by name, and ROUND tidies the percentage.
AND inside IF lets a rating depend on more than one condition.

blocks.text: Well done: you can now build a working store scorecard. Revisit any mission to sharpen a skill.

items.prompt: Cells A2:A4 hold Nairobi, Mombasa, Nairobi and C2:C4 hold 100, 80, 50 (sales in K). What does =SUMIFS(C2:C4,A2:A4,"Nairobi") return, in K?
A store's four weekly sales in K are 120, 95, 100 and 130. How many weeks does =COUNTIFS(C2:C5,">="&100) count?
Why fetch each store's target with XLOOKUP instead of typing the target into the scorecard?

options.label: The target comes from the table by store name, so one change in the table updates the scorecard
Typed numbers are not allowed in Excel
XLOOKUP rounds the target to 1 decimal place
XLOOKUP sorts the stores from best to worst

items.prompt: Rules: Star needs achievement at or above 100% AND at least 3 good weeks; otherwise Watch if achievement is at least 90%; otherwise Action. A store has achievement 102% and 2 good weeks. What rating does =IF(AND(L2>=100,J2>=3),"Star",IF(L2>=90,"Watch","Action")) give?
